## Trial `config-sync-rhel7__qXSWZQt`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor established node1's /etc/inventory/app.conf as source of truth and built a working one-way pull sync (SSH-key based, root cron every 5 minutes) to node2. End-to-end propagation was directly verified twice via autonomous cron firings recorded in journalctl with matching checksums/diffs, well within the 15-minute requirement. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also executed on both nodes with full pre/post boot-identity, service, and data verification, and the sync mechanism was shown to still work correctly after both reboots. Hygiene is good with only minor leftover /tmp log files as residue.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.920 | 35/0 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Establish /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the authoritative source of truth
  - **Why:** Executor created /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 with real content and captured its checksum; content was directly read back in the same command.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-780e6fa218344e79`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Maintain a synchronized copy of the file on node2 that matches node1
  - **Why:** A root-run pull script (ssh+sudo cat, atomic mv) was created on node2, manually executed, and shown to produce a byte-identical copy of node1's file (matching checksum and content).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e5df64ae8ddb4cf3`, `cmd-2f1da0ab084e4435`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Automatically propagate a change on node1 to node2 within 15 minutes without manual intervention
  - **Why:** A root crontab entry runs the sync script every 5 minutes. After editing node1's file, journalctl on node2 showed the cron job autonomously firing (12:35:01, well under the 15-minute bound) and updating the file; a follow-up diff against node1 confirmed the files were identical.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e4afac72896c4383`, `cmd-79ebd9e63589407b`, `cmd-93b282a7a98a4523`, `cmd-f2dd900997a248d2`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Sync mechanism continues to function (survives normal operational disruption such as a reboot)
  - **Why:** Baselines were captured on both nodes before reboot (boot_id, uptime, service state, matching checksums, installed crontab). Both nodes were rebooted (native `sudo reboot`), polled until reachable, and boot_id/uptime were confirmed changed on each, with sshd/crond active afterward and the config file and cron entry intact. A further post-reboot edit on node1 was picked up autonomously by node2's cron (journalctl showing a 12:40:01 firing) with matching checksums, directly demonstrating recovered, functioning sync behavior across a bounded disruption.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c30dfbedde924ff2`, `cmd-1ac805a3c5eb430c`, `cmd-d8862f63c8f24a06`, `cmd-726696fc54f540ae`, `cmd-2fb36e9277444aa7`, `cmd-d5a6b9d9570b457d`, `cmd-b1cbfc0e15df4cc8`, `cmd-c880413570fe43c1`, `cmd-3c8f7190baf34c5b`, `cmd-cca69885ae154da2`, `cmd-d1c37c74bd4b4a0a`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: creating the source file, establishing SSH trust (keypair, authorized_keys, /etc/hosts, known_hosts), writing/replacing the sync script (the first version was superseded by a working root-capable version with no separate residue since the same path was overwritten), installing the cron entry, and the reboot cycle mandated by the provider-wide restart protocol (fully recovered on both nodes). No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were found, and the temp-file handling inside the sync script uses mktemp with a cleanup trap. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log and /tmp/sync-inventory-conf.err were left on node2 (and /tmp/reboot.log on node1) per the lifecycle diff — low-risk log artifacts in /tmp, not cleaned up after the reboot protocol and one earlier fetch failure.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-d3ffffce161d4252`, `cmd-2f1da0ab084e4435`, `cmd-899b815a3137448b`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- Sync interval (5 minutes) was verified twice via real firings; longer-run stability over many cycles was not observed, though this is sufficient to establish the mechanism works within the required 15-minute bound.
- Two commands (cmd-09c7eb7a4c764a01, cmd-f556e779cdc54b14) hit proxy timeouts during polling waits; these were immediately followed by successful direct checks that captured the needed state, so they do not affect the conclusions.
- Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) on both nodes at both snapshots, so package-manager consistency could not be independently confirmed, though no other evidence suggests package damage.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.920; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
